_purpose: Canonical machine-readable statement of HMTc Method v2.0. This is the single source of truth for how limit selection and post-publication tightening are described across heavymetalcertified.com. The August 2026 Program Manual controls: initial certification limits are government-limit-only; the retired P97/P45 pathways never select a compliance value; the separate Standards Ratchet may later tighten a published limit from eligible HMTc certified-lot data.
label: HMTc Method v2.0 — government-limit-only
authority: HMTc Infant and Child Foods Program Manual 2026, Parts 1, 2, and 5
supersedes: The selective-occurrence variant previously described under the same version label, including P97/P45 selection and literature-baseline rationale tags.

statement.default: For each product and analyte, use the strictest applicable maximum level set by a credible sovereign government, converted to the product's native basis.
statement.formulation_split: Where a government instrument splits a limit by product form or formulation, adopt that split and cite it.
statement.unregulated_cell: Where no government regulates the exact cell, use a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value; where the analyte is not material in the matrix, publish an n/m determination with its control method.
statement.occurrence_boundary: Heavy Metal Index occurrence evidence is contextual only. It may support category characterization, prioritization, surveillance, and review, but it has no role in initial limit selection or certification status.
statement.status: Status is determined from MaxPoL against the current published HMTc limit and by nothing else. The initial published limit is government-derived; a later ratcheted limit may be lower.
statement.basis: The 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion applies only within infant formula. Other product forms take the government value in the applicable native basis without an invented conversion.
statement.alara: ALARA remains an enforceable operating principle implemented through surveillance, CAPA, Status B improvement obligations, supplier and process controls, and the separate Standards Ratchet; it is not an initial occurrence-based limit-selection formula.
statement.ratchet: After publication, the Standards Ratchet uses eligible HMTc certified-lot results. It fires for an analyte only when, for two consecutive annual reviews, the P80 of the capped combined Status A and Status B trigger pool is at or below 80% of the current limit and at least 50% of SKUs in that pool have qualifying lots at or below 60% of the current limit. The new limit is the greater of the Status A P80 or 80% of the current limit, so no event lowers a limit by more than 20%; transition is 12–18 months.
